title: Godless: The Church of Liberalism
author: Ann Coulter
target_audience: Individuals interested in American politics and culture wars
Readers seeking polemical and provocative social commentary
core_themes: Liberalism as a secular belief system
Critique of left-wing ideology and policy
Religion and its place in public life
Education, science, and the culture war
Political polarization in the United States
primary_purpose: To argue that American liberalism functions as a dogmatic, secular religion, criticizing its influence on policy, culture, education, and science, while mobilizing conservative readers against what the author perceives as liberal excesses and hypocrisies.

structure_format.narrative_style: Polemical, satirical, confrontational, and heavily opinion-driven
structure_format.organization: Divided into themed chapters focusing on different aspects of liberalism (e.g., education, science, secularism, morality)
features: Extensive use of sarcasm and hyperbole
Frequent references to current events and political figures as of the mid-2000s

key_concepts_lessons: Liberalism can be seen as a substitute religion rooted in faith rather than reason.
Secularization in education and public institutions is heavily critiqued, especially the exclusion of religious ideas.
Defenders of evolution and science are likened to religious adherents dogmatically defending their beliefs.
Liberal activists and politicians are accused of hypocrisy and moral relativism.
The media, academia, and courts are presented as complicit in advancing a liberal agenda.
notable_features: Controversial analogies equating liberalism with organized religion
Frequent use of caustic humor and rhetorical exaggeration
Appeals to conservative ideologies and talking points
Heavy criticism of high-profile liberal figures and institutions
cultural_historical_context: Published in 2006, during the George W. Bush presidency, against a backdrop of heightened polarization in American politics, post-9/11 debates on religion in public life, disputes over science education (especially evolution), and growing divisions over social values.
reception_impact: New York Times bestseller and widely discussed in conservative media circles
Praised by fans for its bold critiques and wit
Highly controversial and condemned by liberal commentators and some moderates for what they considered inflammatory, inaccurate, or divisive arguments
Contributed to the culture war rhetoric and polarized public discourse
